title: Get started
description: Install the core SDK and one provider, then create a sandbox from TypeScript or Go.
---

Sandbox Kit is a client for cloud sandboxes. You install the core package and one provider, Daytona or Modal, and call the same client in TypeScript or Go.

Pick the provider you already have an account with. The snippets on every page have a **TypeScript** tab and a **Go** tab. The choice is saved in this browser.

<Cards>
  <Card title="Daytona" href="/docs/daytona" description="An API key. Create from the default snapshot." />
  <Card title="Modal" href="/docs/modal" description="A token pair and an existing app. Create from a container image." />
</Cards>

## What you install

| | Core package | Provider package |
| --- | --- | --- |
| TypeScript | `@sandbox-kit/sandbox` | `@sandbox-kit/daytona` or `@sandbox-kit/modal` |
| Go | `github.com/sandbox-kit/kit/sdks/go/sandbox` | `.../providers/daytona` or `.../providers/modal` |

TypeScript needs Node.js 20, 22, or 24.15+. Go needs Go 1.26.0 or later.

Install only the provider you use. The core package is the client. The provider package connects that client to Daytona or Modal.

<Callout title="Closing the client leaves the sandbox running">
`client.close()` and `Client.Close` release the connection in your process. They do not stop, terminate, archive, or delete the sandbox. Shut the sandbox down from the [lifecycle](/docs/lifecycle) page, or set a lifetime when you create it.
</Callout>

A client that constructs successfully has not checked your credentials. Daytona or Modal checks them on the first request.

---
title: Daytona
description: Install the Daytona provider, set an API key, and create a sandbox from the default snapshot.
---

Daytona sandboxes start from a snapshot. With no create options, Sandbox Kit uses the default snapshot for your target.

You need a Daytona API key. This release talks to Daytona SDK v0.225.0.

## Install

<Tabs groupId="language" items={['TypeScript', 'Go']} persist>
  <Tab value="TypeScript">

Node.js 20, 22, or 24.15+.

```sh
npm install @sandbox-kit/sandbox @sandbox-kit/daytona
```

  </Tab>
  <Tab value="Go">

Go 1.26.0 or later.

```sh
go get github.com/sandbox-kit/kit/sdks/go/sandbox@latest
go get github.com/sandbox-kit/kit/sdks/go/providers/daytona@latest
```

  </Tab>
</Tabs>

## Create a sandbox

Set `DAYTONA_API_KEY`, then run this program. It creates one sandbox and prints the id.

<Tabs groupId="language" items={['TypeScript', 'Go']} persist>
  <Tab value="TypeScript">

```ts
import { daytona } from "@sandbox-kit/daytona";
import { Client } from "@sandbox-kit/sandbox";

await using client = new Client({
  provider: daytona(),
  auth: { apiKey: { key: process.env.DAYTONA_API_KEY! } },
  timeout: 120_000,
});

const sandbox = await client.create();
console.log(sandbox.id);
```

`timeout` is milliseconds. `await using` closes the client when the block ends. If that syntax is unavailable, call `await client.close()` in a `finally` block.

  </Tab>
  <Tab value="Go">

```go
package main

import (
	"context"
	"fmt"
	"os"
	"time"

	"github.com/sandbox-kit/kit/sdks/go/providers/daytona"
	"github.com/sandbox-kit/kit/sdks/go/sandbox"
)

func main() {
	client, err := sandbox.NewClient(daytona.New(), &sandbox.Config{
		Auth: &sandbox.AuthConfig{Credentials: &sandbox.APIKey{
			ApiKey: &sandbox.APIKeyCredentials{Key: os.Getenv("DAYTONA_API_KEY")},
		}},
		Timeout: sandbox.Duration(2 * time.Minute),
	})
	if err != nil {
		panic(err)
	}
	defer client.Close(context.Background())

	instance, err := client.Create(context.Background(), nil)
	if err != nil {
		panic(err)
	}
	fmt.Println(instance.ID())
}
```

A nil create request uses the default snapshot. `Timeout` is a Go duration.

  </Tab>
</Tabs>

Omit `auth` when the Daytona SDK should use credentials it already finds in the environment.

## Optional settings

| Setting | TypeScript | Go |
| --- | --- | --- |
| API URL | `endpoint` | `Config.Endpoint` with `sandbox.Value` |
| Target | `region` | `Config.Region` with `sandbox.Value` |
| Organization | `scope: { organizationId }` | `Scope.OrganizationId` |

The default API URL is `https://app.daytona.io/api`. A remote URL must be HTTPS. HTTP is accepted for localhost and loopback addresses. Sandbox Kit does not read a Daytona URL from the environment. Set `endpoint` on the client when you need a different one.

A bearer token is `auth: { bearerToken: { token } }` in TypeScript and `BearerToken` in Go. That credential requires an organization id.

## What you can do next

Create from a named snapshot or a container image, and set CPU, memory, disk, labels, network, and lifetime policies on the [create](/docs/create) page.

On a sandbox you already have, call `get` with its id, then start, stop, pause, archive, or delete it. See [Manage a sandbox](/docs/lifecycle).

CPU is a whole number of cores. Memory and disk are a whole number of GiB, written as MiB (`4096` is 4 GiB). A size override requires an image. A snapshot create keeps the snapshot's size.

Runnable project: [create-daytona-sandbox](https://github.com/sandbox-kit/kit/tree/main/examples/typescript/daytona/create-daytona-sandbox) (TypeScript) and [the Go project](https://github.com/sandbox-kit/kit/tree/main/examples/go/daytona/create-daytona-sandbox).

---
title: Create a sandbox
description: Choose a snapshot or an image, set a size, and decide how long the sandbox lives.
---

`client.create` in TypeScript and `Client.Create` in Go return a handle. The handle's id is the sandbox you just created. Fields you leave out keep the provider's default. A field the provider does not support fails in the client, before the provider is called.

Switch provider to see the create call you will run. The language tab is the same one you picked on the setup pages.

<Tabs groupId="provider" items={['Daytona', 'Modal']} persist>
  <Tab value="Daytona">

A call with no options uses the default snapshot. To pick an image and a size, pass both. CPU is a whole number of cores. Memory and disk are whole GiB written as MiB, so 4 GiB is `4096`.

<Tabs groupId="language" items={['TypeScript', 'Go']} persist>
  <Tab value="TypeScript">

```ts
const sandbox = await client.create({
  source: { image: { reference: "daytonaio/playground:latest" } },
  resources: {
    cpuCores: 2,
    memoryMib: 4096n,
    diskMib: 8192n,
  },
  runtime: { language: "typescript" },
});
```

Durations on the create request are milliseconds. A missing property means "leave the provider default."

  </Tab>
  <Tab value="Go">

```go
instance, err = client.Create(ctx, &sandbox.CreateOptions{
	Source: &sandbox.SandboxSource{Kind: &sandbox.Image{
		Image: &sandbox.ImageSource{Reference: "daytonaio/playground:latest"},
	}},
	Resources: &sandbox.Resources{
		CpuCores:  sandbox.Value(2.0),
		MemoryMib: sandbox.Value(uint64(4096)),
		DiskMib:   sandbox.Value(uint64(8192)),
	},
})
```

`sandbox.Value` marks an optional number as set, including zero. `sandbox.Duration` sets a timeout or a delay.

  </Tab>
</Tabs>

You can also name a snapshot, set labels, egress allowlists, secrets, a TTL, and stop, pause, archive, or delete policies. A linked sandbox must be ephemeral. The client rejects that request otherwise.

Set the Daytona target with `region` on the client. A placement block on the create request is rejected.

  </Tab>
  <Tab value="Modal">

Pass a registry image. The app name belongs on the client, not on this request. CPU can be fractional, from 0.125 in steps of 0.001. Memory is MiB, at least 128 when you set it.

<Tabs groupId="language" items={['TypeScript', 'Go']} persist>
  <Tab value="TypeScript">

```ts
const sandbox = await client.create({
  source: { image: { reference: "alpine:3.21" } },
  resources: { cpuCores: 0.5, memoryMib: 512n },
  runtime: {
    workingDirectory: "/tmp",
    entrypoint: ["sleep", "infinity"],
  },
  lifetime: {
    maximumLifetime: 5 * 60_000,
    idleTerminate: { mode: "after", after: 60_000 },
  },
});
```

`maximumLifetime` and `after` are milliseconds.

  </Tab>
  <Tab value="Go">

```go
instance, err = client.Create(ctx, &sandbox.CreateOptions{
	Source: &sandbox.SandboxSource{Kind: &sandbox.Image{
		Image: &sandbox.ImageSource{Reference: "alpine:3.21"},
	}},
	Resources: &sandbox.Resources{
		CpuCores:  sandbox.Value(0.5),
		MemoryMib: sandbox.Value(uint64(512)),
	},
	Lifetime: &sandbox.LifetimePolicy{
		MaximumLifetime: sandbox.Duration(5 * time.Minute),
	},
})
```

  </Tab>
</Tabs>

You can also set gVisor or a Linux VM, cloud and region, ports, secrets, labels, and a readiness check. A ready wait needs a probe and a positive timeout.

Modal does not accept a disk size, an API endpoint, or Daytona-style stop and archive policies. Those fields fail before the call.

  </Tab>
</Tabs>

## Units

| | Daytona | Modal |
| --- | --- | --- |
| CPU | Whole cores | Fractional cores, minimum 0.125, step 0.001 |
| Memory | Whole GiB, written as MiB | MiB, minimum 128 when set |
| Disk | Whole GiB, written as MiB | Cannot be set at create time |
| Timeouts in TypeScript | Milliseconds | Milliseconds |
| Timeouts in Go | `sandbox.Duration` | `sandbox.Duration` |

Account quotas, image names, regions, and capacity are checked by the provider. The client checks shape: known values, bounds, and combinations it can reject locally.

`Info()` on the handle is a copy of the metadata the provider returned. Editing that copy does not change the sandbox. Reported CPU and memory can differ from the numbers you sent.

In-sandbox commands, GPU requests, resizing, extra storage, and browsers are outside this client. Create covers the sandbox itself.

---
title: Configure the client
description: Pass auth, a timeout, and provider scope when you construct the client.
---

Construct the client once. Later edits to the object you passed in do not change the client that is already running.

<Tabs groupId="provider" items={['Daytona', 'Modal']} persist>
  <Tab value="Daytona">

<Tabs groupId="language" items={['TypeScript', 'Go']} persist>
  <Tab value="TypeScript">

```ts
await using client = new Client({
  provider: daytona(),
  auth: { apiKey: { key: process.env.DAYTONA_API_KEY! } },
  region: "us",
  timeout: 120_000,
});
```

`timeout` is the default deadline for later calls, in milliseconds. Pass one auth shape: `apiKey`, `bearerToken`, or `oauthRefresh`.

  </Tab>
  <Tab value="Go">

```go
client, err := sandbox.NewClient(daytona.New(), &sandbox.Config{
	Auth: &sandbox.AuthConfig{Credentials: &sandbox.APIKey{
		ApiKey: &sandbox.APIKeyCredentials{Key: os.Getenv("DAYTONA_API_KEY")},
	}},
	Region:  sandbox.Value("us"),
	Timeout: sandbox.Duration(2 * time.Minute),
})
```

Go returns `(*Client, error)`. An invalid config fails here, before any sandbox exists.

  </Tab>
</Tabs>

| Setting | What to pass |
| --- | --- |
| API key | `auth.apiKey.key` / `APIKey` |
| Bearer token | `auth.bearerToken.token` / `BearerToken`, plus an organization id |
| Endpoint | `endpoint` / `Config.Endpoint`. Default `https://app.daytona.io/api` |
| Target | `region` / `Config.Region` |
| Organization | `scope.organizationId` / `Scope.OrganizationId` |

A remote endpoint uses HTTPS. HTTP is accepted for localhost and loopback. A URL with a username, password, or fragment is rejected.

  </Tab>
  <Tab value="Modal">

<Tabs groupId="language" items={['TypeScript', 'Go']} persist>
  <Tab value="TypeScript">

```ts
await using client = new Client({
  provider: modal(),
  auth: {
    tokenPair: {
      id: process.env.MODAL_TOKEN_ID!,
      secret: process.env.MODAL_TOKEN_SECRET!,
    },
  },
  scope: {
    appName: process.env.MODAL_APP_NAME!,
    environment: "main",
  },
  region: "us-east",
  timeout: 120_000,
});
```

`region` is the default placement. You can still set cloud and region on a single create request.

  </Tab>
  <Tab value="Go">

```go
client, err := sandbox.NewClient(modal.New(), &sandbox.Config{
	Auth: &sandbox.AuthConfig{Credentials: &sandbox.TokenPair{
		TokenPair: &sandbox.TokenPairCredentials{
			Id:     os.Getenv("MODAL_TOKEN_ID"),
			Secret: os.Getenv("MODAL_TOKEN_SECRET"),
		},
	}},
	Scope: &sandbox.Scope{
		AppName:     sandbox.Value(os.Getenv("MODAL_APP_NAME")),
		Environment: sandbox.Value("main"),
	},
	Region:  sandbox.Value("us-east"),
	Timeout: sandbox.Duration(2 * time.Minute),
})
```

  </Tab>
</Tabs>

| Setting | What to pass |
| --- | --- |
| Token pair | `auth.tokenPair` / `TokenPair` |
| OAuth refresh | Client id, plus one client secret or one JWT key |
| App | `scope.appName` / `Scope.AppName`, required |
| Environment | `scope.environment` / `Scope.Environment`, often `main` |
| Region | `region` / `Config.Region` |

`endpoint` is rejected. Modal does not take an API URL on this client.

  </Tab>
</Tabs>

## Timeouts

`timeout` on the client is the default deadline. A create request can override it. A lifecycle call can override it again.

Explicit zero adds no deadline of Sandbox Kit's own. A context deadline or an abort signal that arrives earlier still applies.

Daytona keeps its 60-second default for create, start, stop, pause, and delete when you omit the timeout, and when you pass explicit zero. A Daytona timeout that is not a whole number of seconds is rejected.

## Credentials

Keep the config object out of logs. It holds secrets. A TypeScript config is a plain object, so `JSON.stringify` includes those fields.

Construction does not contact the provider. A wrong key fails on the first create, get, or attach. Read that failure on the [errors](/docs/errors) page.

title: Examples
description: Run one project for the provider and the operation you need. Each project loads its own environment file.
---

The example projects live in the Sandbox Kit repository. Each one selects one provider, loads a `.env` file, and performs one operation.

## Run one

TypeScript needs Node.js 20, 22, or 24.15+. Go needs Go 1.26.0 or later.

<Tabs groupId="language" items={['TypeScript', 'Go']} persist>
  <Tab value="TypeScript">

```sh
git clone https://github.com/sandbox-kit/kit.git
cd kit/examples/typescript/daytona/create-daytona-sandbox
cp .env.example .env
npm install && npm run build && npm start
```

Put `DAYTONA_API_KEY` in `.env`. For Modal, start from `examples/typescript/modal/create-modal-sandbox` and set the token pair and app name.

  </Tab>
  <Tab value="Go">

```sh
git clone https://github.com/sandbox-kit/kit.git
cd kit/examples/go/daytona/create-daytona-sandbox
cp .env.example .env
go run .
```

Put `DAYTONA_API_KEY` in `.env`. For Modal, start from `examples/go/modal/create-modal-sandbox`.

  </Tab>
</Tabs>

Creation projects provision a real sandbox. Lifecycle projects use the sandbox id in `.env`. Stop, terminate, archive, and delete can destroy that sandbox. Error projects fail locally and create nothing.

Skip `cp .env.example` when you already have a `.env`.

## Daytona

| Operation | TypeScript | Go |

title: Daytona
description: Install the Daytona provider, set an API key, and create a sandbox.
---

A Daytona sandbox starts from a snapshot. Pass no create options and Sandbox Kit uses the default snapshot for your target. You need a Daytona API key. This client talks to Daytona SDK v0.225.0.

## Install

<Tabs groupId="language" items={['TypeScript', 'Go']} persist>
  <Tab value="TypeScript">

```sh
npm install @sandbox-kit/sandbox @sandbox-kit/daytona
```

  </Tab>
  <Tab value="Go">

```sh
go get github.com/sandbox-kit/kit/sdks/go/sandbox@latest
go get github.com/sandbox-kit/kit/sdks/go/providers/daytona@latest
```

  </Tab>
</Tabs>

## Create a sandbox

Set `DAYTONA_API_KEY`. This program creates one sandbox and prints its id.

<Tabs groupId="language" items={['TypeScript', 'Go']} persist>
  <Tab value="TypeScript">

```ts
import { daytona } from "@sandbox-kit/daytona";
import { Client } from "@sandbox-kit/sandbox";

await using client = new Client({
  provider: daytona(),
  auth: { apiKey: { key: process.env.DAYTONA_API_KEY! } },
  timeout: 120_000,
});

const sandbox = await client.create();
console.log(sandbox.id);
```

`timeout` is milliseconds. `await using` closes the client when the block ends. Call `await client.close()` in a `finally` block when that syntax is unavailable.

  </Tab>
  <Tab value="Go">

```go
package main

import (
	"context"
	"fmt"
	"os"
	"time"

	"github.com/sandbox-kit/kit/sdks/go/providers/daytona"
	"github.com/sandbox-kit/kit/sdks/go/sandbox"
)

func main() {
	client, err := sandbox.NewClient(daytona.New(), &sandbox.Config{
		Auth: &sandbox.AuthConfig{Credentials: &sandbox.APIKey{
			ApiKey: &sandbox.APIKeyCredentials{Key: os.Getenv("DAYTONA_API_KEY")},
		}},
		Timeout: sandbox.Duration(2 * time.Minute),
	})
	if err != nil {
		panic(err)
	}
	defer client.Close(context.Background())

	instance, err := client.Create(context.Background(), nil)
	if err != nil {
		panic(err)
	}
	fmt.Println(instance.ID())
}
```

A nil create request uses the default snapshot. `Timeout` is a Go duration.

  </Tab>
</Tabs>

Omit `auth` when the Daytona SDK should use credentials it already finds in the environment. Closing the client here does not delete the sandbox.

| --- | --- | --- |
| API URL | `endpoint` | `Config.Endpoint` |
| Target | `region` | `Config.Region` |
| Organization | `scope.organizationId` | `Scope.OrganizationId` |
| Bearer token | `auth.bearerToken.token` | `BearerToken` |

The default API URL is `https://app.daytona.io/api`. A remote URL must be HTTPS. HTTP is accepted for localhost and loopback. Sandbox Kit does not read the URL from the environment. A bearer token requires an organization id.

In Go, set an optional string with `sandbox.Value`. Full field rules are on [Configure the client](/docs/configuration).

title: Configure the client
description: Set auth, a timeout, a region, and provider scope when you construct the client.
---

Construct the client once, with the provider package and a config object. Later edits to that object do not change the client that is already running. Go returns `(*Client, error)`. TypeScript throws when the config is invalid.

| Field | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `provider` | The provider package, such as `daytona()` or `modal()` |
| `auth` | One credential shape. Omit it to use credentials the provider SDK already has |
| `scope` | App, environment, or organization |
| `endpoint` | Provider API URL, where that provider accepts one |
| `region` | Provider target or default placement |
| `timeout` | Default deadline for later calls |

TypeScript `timeout` is milliseconds. Go `Timeout` is `sandbox.Duration`. Pass one auth shape: `apiKey`, `tokenPair`, `bearerToken`, or `oauthRefresh`.

Build the first client on the [Daytona](/docs/daytona) or [Modal](/docs/modal) page. The sections below are the settings you change.

## Daytona

```ts
await using client = new Client({
  provider: daytona(),
  auth: { apiKey: { key: process.env.DAYTONA_API_KEY! } },
  ...(process.env.DAYTONA_TARGET ? { region: process.env.DAYTONA_TARGET } : {}),
  timeout: 120_000,
});
```

  </Tab>

config := &sandbox.Config{
	Auth: &sandbox.AuthConfig{Credentials: &sandbox.APIKey{
		ApiKey: &sandbox.APIKeyCredentials{Key: os.Getenv("DAYTONA_API_KEY")},
	}},
	Timeout: sandbox.Duration(2 * time.Minute),
}
if target := os.Getenv("DAYTONA_TARGET"); target != "" {

| API key | `auth.apiKey.key` / `APIKey` |
| Bearer token | `auth.bearerToken.token` / `BearerToken`, plus an organization id |
| Endpoint | `endpoint` / `Config.Endpoint`. Default `https://app.daytona.io/api` |
| Target | `region` / `Config.Region`. Leave it unset for the default target |
| Organization | `scope.organizationId` / `Scope.OrganizationId` |

A remote endpoint uses HTTPS. HTTP is accepted for localhost and loopback. A URL with a username, password, or fragment is rejected. Sandbox Kit does not read the Daytona URL from the environment.

## Modal

<Tabs groupId="language" items={['TypeScript', 'Go']} persist>

	Auth: &sandbox.AuthConfig{Credentials: &sandbox.TokenPair{
		TokenPair: &sandbox.TokenPairCredentials{

| --- | --- |
| Token pair | `auth.tokenPair` / `TokenPair` |
| OAuth refresh | Client id, plus one client secret or one JWT key |

## Timeouts

`timeout` on the client is the default deadline. A create request can override it. A lifecycle call can override it again.

Explicit zero adds no deadline of Sandbox Kit's own. A context deadline or an abort signal that arrives earlier still applies.

Daytona keeps its 60-second default for create, start, stop, pause, and delete when you omit the timeout, and when you pass explicit zero. A Daytona timeout that is not a whole number of seconds is rejected.

## Credentials

Keep the config object out of logs. It holds secrets. A TypeScript config is a plain object, so `JSON.stringify` includes those fields.

Construction does not contact the provider. A wrong key fails on the first create, get, or attach. Read that failure in [Read an error](/docs/errors).
